<Rep. Jamie Raskin>: H.R. 1163, the Prove It Act of 2025, is yet another effort by the Republican Majority to hamstring federal agencies and undermine the rules that keep us all safe. Under the guise of helping small businesses, this legislation would, in fact, empower the business lobby to stall and obstruct rules across the board.
The Regulatory Flexibility Act already requires the government to consider the impact on small businesses before promulgating a rule. The Prove It Act, however, would essentially give a veto over every rule to one small office in the Small Business Administration (SBA). The Chief Counsel for Advocacy of the SBA--a position that, in recent years, was deemed so insignificant that it was left vacant for nearly a decade--would now be charged with veto power over every rule proposed by every agency in the federal government. In other words, the same Republicans who applaud as President Trump fires thousands of government employees want to vest this one, unelected bureaucrat with broad, unreviewable authority over every other agency in the executive branch.
Moreover, the same Republican colleagues who claim that they have offered this legislation to help small businesses have, in fact, left small businesses out to dry time and time again.
For example, 70% of small businesses report they are facing higher costs for goods and services purchased. In turn, many are passing those increases on to customers with nearly 60% raising their own prices.\1\ President Trump's tariff policy has ``made the leap from protecting domestic production to protecting tech oligarchs''\2\ with huge tech companies lobbying through ``private back channels'' for ``specific tariff exemptions.''\3\ But small businesses do not have global logistics teams and well-paid lobbyists, so they are left to navigate this chaos on their own. As companies pass the cost of these tariffs on to consumers, President Trump's policies will end up resulting in an average loss per household of approximately $2,400--which means less money to spend at local restaurants, shops, and other small businesses in our communities.\4\
\1\Neil Bradley & John G. Murphy, Helping Small Businesses Navigate Tariffs: Seeking Relief, FAQs, U.S. Chamber of Commerce (Aug. 7, 2025), https://www.uschamber.com/small-business/small-business-faq-what-you-need-to-know-about-tariffs.
\2\Tom Wheeler, Trump's tech tariffs: From protecting production to protecting Big Tech's profits (Mar. 10, 2025), The Brookings Institution, https://www.brookings.edu/articles/trumps-tech-tariffs-from-protecting-production-to-protecting-big-techs-profits/.
\3\Lauren Goode, Where Were Big Tech's CEO's on Tariffs?, Wired (Apr. 11, 2025), https://www.wired.com/story/plaintext-tech-ceos-silent-trump-tariffs/.
\4\The Budget Lab at Yale, State of U.S. Tariffs: August 7, 2025 (Aug. 7, 2025), https://budgetlab.yale.edu/research/state-us-tariffs-august-7-2025.
At the same time, the Trump Administration has crippled the agency tasked with helping small businesses sort through these problems. Under Elon Musk and his minions at the Department of Government Efficiency (DOGE), the Administration fired almost half of the SBA's staff and made it nearly impossible for small businesses to get the help they need from the federal government.
After making small businesses eat the cost of the tariffs and after dismantling the one agency that was dedicated to helping small businesses navigate this mess, it is clear that while Republicans say they want to help small businesses, their policies are crushing small businesses and the communities that depend on them.
We can find the real motive for this legislation by looking at the man that Republicans have installed in the role of Chief Counsel at the SBA. Dr. Casey Mulligan, who was recently confirmed in a party line vote, has written extensively about how America has gone wrong since the Franklin Roosevelt Administration. He opposes increasing the minimum wage. He opposes fines for polluters. He opposes sick leave for employees. He believes Congress should repeal the Affordable Care Act--and, failing that, should at least undo protections for patients with pre-existing conditions. He even blamed the 2008 mortgage crisis on unemployment insurance and healthcare subsidies.\5\
\5\Press Release, Senator Edward J. Markey, Ranking Member Markey Votes No on Advancing President Trump's Small Business Nominees (Apr. 2, 2025), https://www.sbc.senate.gov/public/index.cfm/ pressreleases?ID=2AC25BAB-8BD5-4E99-96C8-0334AC4238A0. See also, Letter from Coalition for Sensible Safeguards Opposing the Nomination of Casey Mulligan to Senators Joni Ernst and Edward Markey (Mar. 26, 2025), https://sensiblesafeguards.org/outreach/css-opposes-the-nomination-of-casey-mulligan-as-chief-counsel-of-the-small-business-administrations-office-of-advocacy/.
The Prove It Act would vest this one retrograde economist-- and future appointees like him--with incredible power to undo any regulation he does not like. And he does not like any regulation.
As a result, critical protections for clean air, clean water, safe food, and other lifesaving regulations, including those that protect small businesses, could all be dismantled with the stroke of a pen.
I urge all Members to oppose this dangerous legislation.
Jamie Raskin,
Ranking Member.
